title: Effects of the English language intervention as a foreign language for struggling elementary readers in South Korea: a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether English language interventions improve outcomes for struggling elementary readers in South Korea, and whether effects differ by outcome type, intervention characteristics, classroom context, and grade level. It is a meta-analysis of studies published from 2000 to 2021 that examined English interventions for elementary students identified as underachieving, low achieving, or having learning disabilities.

The authors synthesized 22 studies, separating analyses by study design: 7 between-group experimental/quasi-experimental studies and 15 within-group pre-post studies. The included interventions covered phonics, shared reading, growth mindset, small group instruction, English songs, vocabulary/sentence supports, and related instructional formats. Outcomes were grouped into affective measures such as confidence, motivation, and interest, and achievement measures such as phonological awareness, fluency, vocabulary, reading comprehension, listening comprehension, and writing.

Results showed medium effects for between-group studies and large effects for within-group studies, with substantial heterogeneity. Moderator analyses suggested stronger effects for affective outcomes and several achievement outcomes, with particularly large effects for listening comprehension, letter recognition, and phonological awareness in some subsets. Effects were generally larger for interventions delivered more frequently, across 20–29 sessions or more, and sometimes when teachers were involved. The authors also report larger effects in general education classrooms than inclusion classrooms, and for lower elementary grades than upper grades in the within-group analyses.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system or adaptive instructional system that provides individualized instruction, practice, and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a meta-analysis of English language interventions for struggling elementary readers, not an AI-tool study. No specific AI system is named; the intervention literature is educational reading/English instruction.

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis synthesized 22 experimental and quasi-experimental studies of English language interventions for struggling elementary EFL readers in South Korea. The pooled effects were medium for between-group studies (g=0.684, SE=0.26, CI95=0.18, 1.18; p<0.01) and large for within-group studies (g=1.39, SE=0.67, CI95=0.08, 2.69; p<0.05).
findings.measure: Overall English language intervention effects on English achievement/affective outcomes

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis with a defined search, coding, and random-effects synthesis, so it meets the highest evidence tier for study design. However, it is not an AI-tool evaluation and does not report evidence on generative AI literacy specifically.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effects reported are medium to large (g=0.684 and g=1.39), which qualifies as high impact by the stated threshold. Still, these effects pertain to English intervention generally, not AI literacy or a named AI tool.
